Class ImageProtocol

java.lang.Object
outpututils.ImageProtocol
public class ImageProtocol extends Object
Detects which inline-image protocol, if any, the current terminal is likely to support.

Detection is a best-effort guess based on environment variables (TERM_PROGRAM, TERM, KITTY_WINDOW_ID, ITERM2_SESSION_ID, LC_TERMINAL). A program cannot query the terminal directly, so a result other than ImageProtocol.Protocol.NONE means the terminal usually supports that protocol, not that it is guaranteed to. For example, VS Code sets TERM_PROGRAM=vscode whether or not terminal.integrated.enableImages is turned on.

  • Method Details

    • detectProtocol

      public static ImageProtocol.Protocol detectProtocol()
      Guesses which image protocol the current terminal supports by inspecting environment variables.

      Checks are made in this order, and the first match wins:

      1. Kitty: KITTY_WINDOW_ID is set, TERM_PROGRAM is a known Kitty-compatible terminal, or TERM contains "kitty".
      2. iTerm2: ITERM2_SESSION_ID is set, TERM_PROGRAM is a known iTerm2-compatible terminal, or LC_TERMINAL is "iTerm2".
      3. Sixel: TERM contains "foot", "mlterm", or "yaft", and the terminal is not Apple's Terminal.app.
      4. Otherwise, ImageProtocol.Protocol.NONE.
      Returns:
      the detected ImageProtocol.Protocol, or ImageProtocol.Protocol.NONE if none of the checks match; never null

    • printProtocol

      public static void printProtocol()
      Prints to the terminal which image protocol the terminal is currently using the detectProtocol() method.
